title: Receiver noise, selectivity and overload
blurb: Calculate noise floor from bandwidth, and explain image rejection, roofing filters, attenuators, overload and phase noise.

E4C01.why: Clock **phase noise** combines with strong nearby signals and generates **interference** on the signal you want.
E4C01.trap: Phase noise isn't about calibration or the intercept point.

E4C02.why: A **front-end filter or preselector** acts before the mixer, removing strong out-of-band signals.
E4C02.trap: An IF filter acts after the mixer, too late for front-end overload. A notch removes only one frequency.

E4C03.why: In FM the stronger signal on the same frequency suppresses the weaker: **capture effect**.
E4C03.trap: Desensitization and cross-modulation are other strong-signal effects, not same-frequency FM suppression.

E4C04.why: Noise figure = receiver-generated noise, in dB, **above the theoretical minimum**.
E4C04.trap: It's not compared with atmospheric noise.

E4C05.why: −174 dBm is the thermal noise in **1 Hz** at the input of a **perfect receiver** at room temperature.
E4C05.trap: It's the theoretical minimum, so there's 0 dB of noise figure on top.

E4C06.trap: Take 10 log of the bandwidth ratio (20), not of 10 or 2.

E4C07.why: MDS stands for **minimum discernible signal**, the weakest signal the receiver can detect.

E4C08.why: The A/D converter overloads when the input exceeds its **reference voltage**, its largest input range.

E4C09.why: The image is 2 × IF away. A **high IF** puts it far enough for the front end to remove.
E4C09.trap: A high IF doesn't reduce drift or improve noise figure.

E4C10.why: Set bandwidth to match the **modulation bandwidth**: best signal-to-noise, least interference.
E4C10.trap: Bandwidth doesn't change the RF amplifier's noise figure.

E4C11.why: **Atmospheric noise** is generally above internal noise even after attenuation, so S/N barely changes.
E4C11.trap: An attenuator cuts signal and noise alike; it has no filter.

E4C12.why: A narrow roofing filter **attenuates strong signals near the receive frequency**, improving **blocking dynamic range**.

E4C13.why: **Reciprocal mixing**: oscillator phase noise mixes with a strong adjacent signal and interferes with the wanted one.
E4C13.trap: Two out-of-band signals mixing is intermodulation.

E4C14.why: **IF shift** slides the passband to reduce interference from stations on **adjacent frequencies**.
E4C14.trap: That's RIT or split operation, not IF shift.
